title: She Was the DEA’s Premier Crypto Detective. The Clues Led Straight to Her Own Family
gist: Long Wired profile of Lili Infante, a Russian-born DEA agent who pioneered blockchain-based dark-web investigations: Operation Tornado against Dream Market, then the 2022 takedown of Hydra with IRS investigator Tigran Gambaryan, which led to seizure of about $25 million in bitcoin. The piece interleaves her discovery that her grandmother sold drugs on Hydra and the corruption scandal of her mentor Jose Irizarry.

themes.theme: Crypto as the new laundering paradigm

insights.claim: Infante concluded in 2014 that bitcoin was a perfect cartel tool, because cartels could make transfers online instead of smuggling cash, and that with cryptocurrency the money does not even need to be laundered.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Law enforcement recognized crypto as a laundering rail early; compliance and tracing demand follows.
insights.locator: A clever technology, she thought, and likely also a perfect tool for cartels.

insights.claim: When she searched the DEA case system in 2014, Infante found only one major crypto case, Silk Road, whose founder Ross Ulbricht had been arrested a year earlier, and many colleagues were unaware of or uninterested in it.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Institutional lag in law enforcement against crypto-enabled crime created an opening for early specialists.
insights.locator: But she found only one major case: the Silk Road

insights.claim: Infante's crypto-meetup insight was that every bitcoin transaction is indelibly recorded, so bitcoin is perhaps not anonymous and, once traceable, following the money would be easier than ever.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Public-ledger traceability is the investor-relevant basis for blockchain-analytics and compliance businesses.
insights.locator: The fact that every bitcoin transaction was indelibly recorded

insights.claim: Infante resurrected her undercover persona Olga to pitch Sinaloa Cartel accountants instantaneous digital transactions, because tracing web transactions made crypto the ultimate medium for DEA laundering stings.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Crypto-based stings became a standard investigative playbook.
insights.locator: She resurrected her Olga character

insights.claim: Infante explained that the dark web rested on bitcoin's pseudonymous transactions and the Tor network, which hid IP addresses among many servers, and that dealers were migrating online in droves.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Bitcoin plus Tor shifted drug distribution from street corners to mail-order retail.
insights.locator: The dark web, she explained, relied upon two innovations

insights.claim: A dark-web drug case is the reverse of a typical narcotics investigation: the crime is visible because the drug arrives at your door, but you cannot prove who sent it.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Attribution, not evidence of crime, is the bottleneck, which is why blockchain forensics matters.
insights.locator: A dark-web case, Lili realized, is the exact reverse

insights.claim: Infante spent $200 of DEA money on a Blue Sky marketplace cocaine purchase from vendor HonestCocaine as a proof of concept, and the package arrived with high-quality product.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Tiny test purchases validated the scale of online drug markets for skeptical management.
insights.locator: Lili used a marketplace called Blue Sky

insights.claim: Infante identified vendor Owlcity in February 2016 by asking him to track a missing package; he used USPS.com without Tor, and DEA access to post office web logs led to Chrissano Leslie in Miramar.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Operational-security slips outside Tor, not breaking encryption, unmask dark-web actors.
insights.locator: Finally, in February 2016, Lili had a flash of inspiration.

insights.claim: Dark-web fentanyl and pill traffickers can poison customers unknowingly because they are cut off from users who often overdose alone at home, as in the God Pill case of Joshua Kelly.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Mail-order synthetic opioids create hidden harm clusters with slow detection.
insights.locator: This was a novel threat of drugs delivered through the mail

insights.claim: After Silk Road, Dream Market became the largest US dark-web marketplace, and Infante's Counternarcotics Cyber Task Force named Operation Tornado, after Tor, targeted it, starting with vendors before moving up to administrators OxyMonster and Kitt3n.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Vendor-first investigations are the way into leaderless dark-web organizations.
insights.locator: With the Silk Road gone, a dark-web marketplace known as Dream Market

insights.claim: Infante traced the vendor UStoUS, who sold the 'God Pill' mixing cocaine, amphetamines and fentanyl, to Joshua Kelly's Heady Warez smoke shop in Cape Girardeau, Missouri, and raided it on May 9, 2017.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Postage and IP tracing converted a dark-web handle into a physical raid.
insights.locator: Of Dream’s many vendors, one stood out to Lili

insights.claim: Infante unmasked Dream administrator OxyMonster, Frenchman Gal Vallerius, via a public bitcoin tip wallet address linked to a server also hosting beard-growing sites, then arrested him on arrival at Atlanta airport on August 31, 2017.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Reusing a wallet address and server publicly created the link that identified a top administrator.
insights.locator: Lili discovered OxyMonster’s identity by tracing his bitcoin wallet address

insights.claim: Infante guessed Vallerius's password-protected wallet from personal details such as dates, pets and hobbies and recovered about half a million dollars in bitcoin.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Weak passwords tied to personal data remain a recovery route for investigators.
insights.locator: At home that night, Lili examined Vallerius’ computer.

insights.claim: Hydra was the largest darknet marketplace, with 17 million users and thousands of vendors, and accounted for about 80 percent of the darknet's crypto transactions.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: A single marketplace dominated darknet crypto flows, making it a high-leverage enforcement target.
insights.locator: Hydra was the largest darknet marketplace and among the most sophisticated

insights.claim: Hydra operated like a tech startup with salaried marketers, lawyers, IT staff, an HR department, purity testers and telehealth doctors, and delivered via hidden dead-drop 'klad' caches instead of the mail.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Professionalized criminal platforms scale like startups, with corporate-style operations.
insights.locator: The market, it turned out, employed a diverse roster of salaried professionals

insights.claim: Hydra beat rival RAMP in 2016 using better advertising, wider distribution, Chinese precursor ties, poaching vendors, shutting RAMP's site temporarily, doxing admins and leaking embarrassing screenshots of a 20-year-old RAMP admin.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Darknet competition resembles tech platform wars, including sabotage and reputational attacks.
insights.locator: In 2016, Pavlov found himself in the middle of a digital turf war.

insights.claim: Hydra's money trail ran through exchanges in Moscow's Federation Tower, including Garantex, Suex and Chatex, which the US Treasury later sanctioned for money laundering.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Illicit marketplaces depended on a small set of exchanges, which became sanction targets.
insights.locator: Hydra's money trail ran through Russia's crypto underworld

insights.claim: The US team traced Hydra's central bitcoin wallet to a Hetzner data center in Germany, and on April 5, 2022 German police pulled servers from the facility while Infante presented the Dmitry Pavlov indictment to a San Francisco grand jury, after which Hydra went dark.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Cross-border cooperation and hosting-provider seizures can take down large markets.
insights.locator: On April 5, 2022, the team made its move.

insights.claim: German authorities seized Hydra's bitcoin wallet holding $25 million, and Pavlov was reportedly arrested on April 11, 2022 while fleeing Vologda after Infante bet Russia's FSB would act to avoid embarrassment.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Quantifies the enforcement haul; Russian arrest depended on political embarrassment rather than cooperation.
insights.locator: The Germans, meanwhile, seized the Hydra bitcoin wallet

insights.claim: Russia's February 2022 invasion of Ukraine and NATO sanctions accelerated the Hydra case because the site's crypto exchange could help hackers, arms merchants and private militaries move money into Russia, skirting sanctions.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Sanctions evasion via crypto was a driver of enforcement urgency.
insights.locator: In February 2022, the case suddenly accelerated

insights.claim: Infante posed as a chemist using photos of the DEA's laboratory and got hired by Hydra as a purity tester to help establish jurisdiction.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Undercover infiltration supported jurisdiction for an extraterritorial case.
insights.locator: Lili posed as a chemist and got herself hired by Hydra

insights.claim: IRS investigator Tigran Gambaryan developed the capability to decipher the blockchain and linked corrupt DEA agent Carl Force's theft of more than $700,000 in bitcoin from Silk Road to him, the first time blockchain evidence was introduced in court.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Court acceptance of blockchain evidence underpins legal viability of crypto forensics.
insights.locator: Lili watched Tigran present his investigation

insights.claim: Infante built one of the first interagency cybercrime task forces, drawing in IRS, Postal Inspection, FBI SWAT and Homeland Security, after pitching dark-web dangers to each agency in person.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Multi-agency task forces are how complex crypto cases get resourced.
insights.locator: Almost unintentionally, Lili had formed one of the first interagency cybercrime task forces.

insights.claim: DEA mentor Jose Irizarry later confessed to skimming millions from undercover operations and laundering for cartels while partying with traffickers, with $9 million vanishing, and the AP reported him saying the drug war was a game.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Insider corruption undermined DEA credibility and compromised related casework.
insights.locator: “The drug war’s a game,”

insights.claim: Informant Igor, who took a 20 percent cut of seized proceeds and was rumored to have made millions, was tainted by Irizarry's bust, compromising Infante's crypto laundering stings that depended on his introductions.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Informant-paid-by-seizure incentives created conflicts and operational risk.
insights.locator: he would often take a 20 percent cut of the DEA’s seized proceeds

insights.claim: Infante's grandmother Nina sold marijuana on Hydra after discovering how to use Tor, VPNs and bitcoin, to pay off a gang threatening her grandson Dennis; it was Infante's personal motivation to target Hydra.
insights.speaker: Joshuah Bearman
insights.so_what: Illustrates how deeply Hydra penetrated ordinary Russian society.
insights.locator: Much like Lili, Nina taught herself Tor, VPNs, and bitcoin
